data.title: Yellow nail syndrome — viva
data.summary: Hair & nail disorders · 6 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Yellow nail syndrome** (Hair & nail disorders)_

**Q1. Write a note on yellow nail syndrome (PYQ).**
- Rare disorder with the triad: yellow slow-growing nails, lymphoedema (usually lower limbs) and respiratory involvement (pleural effusion, bronchiectasis, chronic sinusitis, recurrent bronchitis/pneumonia) — two of three features enough for diagnosis
- Adults (median ~50 y); impaired lymphatic drainage (functional lymphatic abnormality) with microvasculopathy

**Q2. Describe the nail changes.**
- Diffusely yellow to yellow-green thickened nails, increased transverse and longitudinal curvature (overcurved), loss of cuticle, absent lunula, onycholysis, very slow growth (<0.25 mm/week; normal ~0.5–1.2 mm), onychomadesis; all 20 nails often affected

**Q3. Associations.**
- Malignancies (lung, breast, lymphoma), autoimmune disease (RA, thyroid), immunodeficiency, nephrotic syndrome, AIDS, drugs (penicillamine, bucillamine, gold, titanium dental implants/joint prostheses — titanium exposure hypothesis)

**Q4. Differential diagnosis of yellow nails.**
- Onychomycosis (KOH/culture), psoriasis, ageing, nicotine staining (proximal spared), carotenaemia (skin also yellow), tetracycline/ antimalarial pigmentation, jaundice (sclera), pachyonychia congenita, nail varnish staining, diabetes (yellowish nails)

**Q5. Investigations.**
- Chest X-ray/HRCT, pleural fluid analysis (exudative, lymphocytic, sometimes chylous), sinus imaging, lymphoscintigraphy, nail clipping KOH/culture, screen for associated malignancy/autoimmunity

**Q6. Treatment.**
- Nails: oral vitamin E (α-tocopherol 800–1200 IU/day) ± oral itraconazole/fluconazole pulse (increase nail growth), zinc, topical vitamin E; nails may improve spontaneously (~30%)
- Lymphoedema: compression, physiotherapy, skin care
- Respiratory: pleurodesis/decortication for recurrent effusions, antibiotics and physiotherapy for bronchiectasis; octreotide (chylous effusions)
- Remove titanium implants if implicated

## Quick spotter facts
- Yellow overcurved slow-growing nails + lymphoedema + pleural effusion — yellow nail syndrome
- Vitamin E + itraconazole

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Nail disorders). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
